correctness.rationale: A fixed-edge DFS exhausts Euler circuits of the binary four-bit de Bruijn graph. Separately, all 2^16 local incoming-to-outgoing pairings are examined, retaining precisely 32-cycles in the edge permutation. Both enumerate identical sets of 2048 rotation classes; every candidate has all 32 length-five windows distinct. Direct cyclic factor enumeration and outward odd/even palindrome-center expansion agree as sets of strings for every candidate. Exact outputs are 22:32,23:32,24:200,27:192,28:920,29:544,30:128 with 51 full palindrome-complexity profiles; 528 symmetry orbits and the rational moments agree with independent recomputation. The standalone code checks the actual accompanying CSV tables. This is exhaustive only for the specified finite domain.

value.rationale: The number of distinct palindromic factors is a standard combinatorial complexity invariant. De Bruijn cycles provide a natural 2048-member complete finite family with all factor sets of lengths one to five identical, so deviations in longer palindromic factors isolate global cyclic arrangement. The exact nonconsecutive spectrum, missing 25 and 26, sharp extrema, 51 full complexity profiles and symmetry decomposition supply substantive finer information not implied by the previously known defining universality or longest-palindrome statistic. The exact tables provide reusable benchmarks for future structural classifications.
